h2: Water Pumps & Filters Kuta & Legian | Bali Fix
intro: Running a guesthouse or long-term villa along Kuta Beach or down in Tuban means dealing with water supply problems that newer areas simply don't face. Water Pumps & Filters Kuta & Legian isn't just a service line — it's what keeps decades-old plumbing functional in salt-heavy coastal air. If your pump cycles non-stop, the rooftop tank won't hold pressure, or tap water tastes off, I can sort it out.

sections.h3: Why Coastal Conditions Wear Pumps and Filters Down Faster
sections.text: Kuta Beach and Legian sit close enough to the ocean that salt-laden air eats through metal fittings within a few seasons. Wells drilled here often pull slightly brackish water, so a proper filtration stage isn't optional — it's what keeps your mixers, heaters and laundry from scaling up. Add decades of original pipework still running under older homes in this area, and you've got a setup where pressure switches seize, pump seals dry out, and rooftop tanks overflow into the lane below.

sections.h3: Typical Calls From Properties in This Stretch
sections.text: The most common jobs I handle for Tuban and Legian properties follow a pattern: the pump kicks on every thirty seconds instead of holding pressure, or water simply stops reaching upper floors after heavy rain floods the drains. Filter cartridges changed once two years ago now turn tap output cloudy and metallic. In multi-room guesthouses, one stuck check valve can leave six bathrooms without hot water by morning.

sections.h3: What to Send on WhatsApp Before I Quote
sections.text: Before I give you a figure, send three things over WhatsApp: a short video of the pump running (or not), a photo of your pressure switch plus any visible corrosion on nearby fittings, and the model label if you can find it. Also tell me how many taps or showers feed off that line, whether the tank is rooftop or ground-level, and roughly when the trouble started. That's enough for me to say whether it's a part swap or a full filter install.

sections.h3: Prevention Habits That Save Headaches Here
sections.text: A few routines make a real difference for villa managers along this coast: flush the whole system after any flooding event so sand doesn't grind into pump impellers, inspect pressure-switch contacts every six months for salt crust, and replace filter cartridges on schedule rather than waiting for taste changes. If your unit sits near Kuta Beach, wrap exposed metal joints in anti-corrosion tape each dry season. Small effort, big payoff over time.

faq.q: How do I know if my pump needs replacing or just a new pressure switch?
faq.a: If the motor hums but no water reaches the tank, it's usually the switch or a seized check valve rather than the pump itself. Send a quick video on WhatsApp and I'll point you in the right direction before any parts are ordered.

faq.q: Can brackish well water be made safe for daily use?
faq.a: Yes — a two-stage cartridge filter handles the mineral content typical of coastal wells around Kuta and Legian. The exact setup depends on your flow rate and what's connected downstream, so I size it after seeing your current layout.

faq.q: How often should rooftop tanks be cleaned in this area?
faq.a: Given the salt air and occasional flooding that stirs up sediment, once every twelve months is sensible for properties in Tuban and Legian. More frequently if you notice discolouration or a musty smell at the taps.
